title: K Most Frequent Values
statement:
Given an array of integers nums and an integer k, return the k values that appear most often in nums.

The tests are built so the answer is unique: the k-th most frequent value always appears strictly more often than the next one. Ties among the chosen values are fine.

Return the values in any order. Aim for better than O(n log n).

examples.why: 9 appears 4 times and 4 appears 3 times. 7 (twice) and 1 (once) are left out. 9 comes last in the array but has the highest count.
5 and 3 both appear 3 times, which is fine because both are chosen. -2 appears only twice.
The only value is the most frequent one.

hints: First you need to know how often each value appears. Which structure gives you that in one pass?
Sorting the distinct values by count works in O(n log n). But a count can never exceed n. How could that bound help?
Make buckets indexed by count: bucket[c] holds every value that appears exactly c times. Read the buckets from the highest count down until you have k values.

explain.intuition:
Step one is always a frequency map: value → count. Step two is picking the k largest counts. Sorting all distinct values by count does it in O(n log n).

The faster idea uses the fact that a count is between 1 and n. Make an array of n + 1 buckets and drop each value into the bucket for its count. Walking the buckets from the top visits values from most to least frequent without any comparison sort, so the whole thing is O(n).
steps: Count how often each value appears with a hash map.
Create n + 1 empty buckets. Put each distinct value into bucket[count].
Walk the buckets from index n down to 1, collecting values.
Stop once you have collected k values and return them.
pitfalls: Returning the first k distinct values in input order instead of the most frequent ones.
Sizing the buckets by the number of distinct values instead of n: a value can appear n times.

solutions.title: Count, then sort by count
solutions.idea: Build the frequency map, sort the distinct values by count descending and take the first k.
solutions.time: O(n + d log d), d = distinct values

solutions.title: Bucket by count
solutions.idea: A count is at most n, so index buckets by count and read them from the top. No comparison sort.

followups: Solve it with a min-heap of size k. When is that better than buckets?
The numbers arrive as an endless stream and you must report the top k at any moment. What would you keep?
